cells.tense: You are naming the whole shape of a thing and still standing inside it while you do.
cells.ask: Tell one person the pattern you see and where it came from, then let them take it or leave it.
cells.core:
You can stand outside something you're in the middle of and say what it is. The pieces sit together in view, and saying it out loud doesn't pull you out of the room it's about.

That's why the small practical move in front of you isn't hard to pick up. You're holding a pattern and a first step at once, and they don't fight. What you see of the whole is real, and the first concrete piece is already in your hand. Seeing it whole keeps you steady while you make the first move, and that steadiness keeps the move honest.

cells.tense: You will have run the whole thing through to its end before it has a chance to start.
cells.ask: Pick the smallest real first step and take it today, before the shape of it comes clear. Let what happens be the next thing you know.
cells.core:
You catch the shape of a thing fast, and then you keep going — every later stage, every turn it will take, all of it already decided up there. Lately the pattern-reading hasn't been taking in what's here. It's been forecasting what's next.

Beginning, actually beginning, is the one move that needs you to touch the first real piece before you know how it lands. If you keep holding out for the finished picture, the seed goes into the drawer and the year goes by. The cost isn't that you're good at seeing ahead. It's that the first step keeps waiting for a picture that isn't coming.

So take one small, actual first step today. Not the plan for it. The step.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that closed behind you, and you haven't turned back around.
cells.ask: Say one thing you notice about a situation you're in, plainly, where someone can hear it. The next sentence doesn't have to be right.
cells.core:
You can see how the pieces of a thing move together. Lately you don't say so. The pattern comes into view and then nothing comes out of your mouth, and the people around you don't hear what you spotted.

What's not in the room is the saying, not the ability — that part still works. There's no debt to settle tonight about why it went quiet.

Try naming one thing you notice about something you're in the middle of. Not a verdict. Just what you see, out loud. If this lands off, the sentence still asks almost nothing of you but a minute.

cells.tense: You are already the one reading the room, and the way you talk about it makes the room sound like it read itself.
cells.ask: After the next read you make, say it once to yourself or out loud — those are the words you choose — and the same read carries you on it.
cells.core:
This is happening now. You catch the shape of something before anyone finishes laying out the parts — the pattern is already in view. But when it gets said, it comes out as what's obvious, what the room already knew, just the way things are. The reading is running. The name on it isn't.

Nothing has to be rebuilt. The ability was gone from view, not from you. What you can do is small and it changes what this is free to start next: after the next time you read something and let it stand as the room's, take one of those reads. Say it's yours. Out loud, once, in the ordinary voice you'd use for a thing you did.
